newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sends more planes for Cambodia evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sends more planes for Cambodia evacuation.

text.p: Singapore will send two more planes to Cambodia on Wednesday to carry out an evacuation operation, the government said.

Singapore sent four air force C-130 aircraft to Phnom Penh airport in the morning, and was sending the other two in the afternoon, a joint Ministry of Defence and Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement said.

"This exercise was in response to requests from Singaporeans who were stranded with their families in Cambodia and who wanted to leave Phnom Penh because of the deterioration of the situation there," the statement said.
The exercise was aimed at evacuating about 300 Singaporeans, and some foreigners, from Cambodia, a source close to the operation told Reuters.
"The evacuation will take place throughout the day until all the Singaporeans who want to leave Cambodia are evacuated," the source said.
"Our first priority is to evacuate Singaporeans. But usually we give allowance for that (evacuation of foreigners)," the source said.
Among the foreigners expected are a group of Bruneians who "have indicated they would like to be included" in the evacuation, the source said.
State television earlier reported the family of the Brunei ambassador to Cambodia would be among those evacuated.
Fighting between rival factions of the country's co-prime ministers flared up in Cambodia over the weekend.
